external.name: External plugins
external.description: Out-of-process third-party plugins: registration, permissions and lifecycle.

external.title: External plugins
external.subtitle: Third-party plugins running as separate containers next to this instance.
external.empty: No external plugins are registered yet. Generate an install token and set it in the plugin container's environment to begin.

installToken.title: One-time install token
installToken.hint: Set this as MK_INSTALL_TOKEN (with MK_CORE_URL) in the plugin container's environment and start it. The token is shown once and expires in 24 hours.
installToken.purpose: The way in for a container you cannot pair by hand: a headless install, a container on another host, one started by a script. It installs a PLUGIN — it is not a credential for an outside client, those live in Tokens.
installToken.step1: Generate the token below. It is shown once and expires in 24 hours.
installToken.step2: Set it as MK_INSTALL_TOKEN, together with MK_CORE_URL, in the plugin container's environment.
installToken.step3: Start the container: it registers itself and shows up here for your approval.

connectionTokens.title: Connection tokens
connectionTokens.hint: Long-lived credentials an outside client — an MCP client, a script — presents to this instance's external API. A token acts as you, capped by its access ceiling; revoke it to cut the connection off. Each user sees only the tokens they issued.
connectionTokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke “{label}”? Clients using it lose access immediately.
connectionTokens.issuedHint: Give this to the connecting client (Authorization: Bearer …). It is shown once and never expires — revoke it here when it is no longer needed.

ceilingHint.read-only: Queries only; nothing can be changed.
ceilingHint.read-write: May add and update data, never delete.
ceilingHint.destructive: May also delete data. Issue only for a client you fully trust.

connectionTokens.destructiveWarning: This token will be able to DELETE data as you. The connected client still confirms each deletion, but a leaked token is a deletion credential.
connectionTokens.installTokenElsewhere: Installing a plugin needs the install token, which lives with pairing.

card.assistantHint: The assistant may call this plugin's tools. It can pass them any data it can read.
card.disabledNoSettings: The plugin is off: its screens, its tools and its settings are unavailable until you switch it back on. Nothing it stored is lost.

confirm.reject: Reject and remove the registration of “{name}”?
confirm.uninstall: Uninstall “{name}”? All of its tokens are revoked immediately.
confirm.purgeOption: Also ask the plugin to erase its own data

api.register: Self-registration endpoint for external plugin containers
api.list: List registered external plugins with their grants and pending updates
api.installToken: Generate a one-time install token for a new external plugin
api.approve: Approve a pending installation or a pending permission-expanding update
api.reject: Reject a pending installation (removes it) or dismiss a pending update
api.setEnabled: Enable or disable an external plugin
api.uninstall: Uninstall an external plugin, revoking all of its tokens first
api.shell: Shell projection of installed external plugins (nav, widgets, screens, i18n)
api.render: Render one screen of an external plugin through the signed proxy
api.action: Run a user action on an external plugin screen
api.operations: List the operations the calling external plugin's grants allow
api.invoke: Invoke one capability-layer operation on the scoped surface
api.metrics: Read a cross-scope per-day metric series (instance surface)
api.metricKeys: List available metric keys for a plugin (instance surface)
api.notifyChanged: Invalidate an external plugin screen for its scope (realtime nudge)
api.deadLetters: List webhook deliveries that exhausted their retries for a plugin
api.redeliver: Queue a dead webhook delivery for another attempt
api.setAssistantEnabled: Allow or forbid an external plugin's tools in the assistant
api.capability: Invoke a capability offered by another plugin (relayed opaquely)
api.deferredBlobs: List exchange blocks waiting for a plugin that is not installed
api.tokens: Exchange a plugin's registration secret for its current background tokens
api.announce: Anonymous announce from a running plugin container (pairing window only)
api.claim: Collect the issued secret after an admin paired this container
api.pairingStatus: Whether the pairing window is open
api.openPairing: Open the pairing window so running containers can announce themselves
api.pair: Pair a candidate by the code it printed to its own log
api.dismissCandidate: Dismiss a candidate without pairing it
api.ignoreCandidate: Ignore a candidate so its container stops appearing
api.unignoreCandidate: Stop ignoring a candidate; it returns on its next announce
api.budgets: Effective per-surface time budgets with the code defaults
api.pubResolve: Routing oracle for the nginx public-path proxy (auth_request sub-requests only)
api.createConnectionToken: Issue a long-lived connection token with an access ceiling

errors.capabilityUnavailable: That capability is not available right now

render.actionFailed: The action could not be completed
render.empty: This screen has nothing to show yet.
render.unauthorized: The container for “{plugin}” is running but does not hold this installation’s secret — its own state was lost. Pair it again from Settings → External plugins: its permissions, its assistant consent and its data stay as they are.

discovery.title: Discovered containers
discovery.openHint: Opens a 15-minute window during which running plugin containers can announce themselves. Anything they say about themselves is unverified until you enter their pairing code.
discovery.none: No containers have announced themselves yet. Start the plugin's container with MK_CORE_URL pointing here — it needs no token.
discovery.codeLabel: Pairing code from the container's log
discovery.conflict: A plugin with this id is already installed. Pairing hands that installation to THIS container: it gets a new secret and this address, and keeps the permissions, the assistant consent and the data the installed one had. That is how a container comes back after losing its own state — and how a different container could take its place, so only do it for one you recognise.
discovery.paired: Container paired — now review its permissions below
discovery.knocking: {count} container(s) tried to connect while pairing was closed. Open the pairing window — they keep retrying, no restart needed.
discovery.ignored: Candidate ignored — its container stops appearing here
discovery.unignored: No longer ignored — it returns on its next announce
discovery.closedHint: Open the pairing window to let running plugin containers announce themselves. It stays open for 15 minutes.

budgets.title: Time budgets
budgets.hint: How long this instance waits for a plugin container on each surface before the call counts as a miss. Milliseconds; guest surfaces (widgets, slots) should stay tight.

connect.title: Connect
connect.description: Pair a running container or hand out an install token, then approve what it asks for.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: How long this instance waits for a plugin container.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.description: Long-lived credentials for outside clients — MCP clients, scripts.

connected.title: Connected
connected.description: Installed plugins, their consents and their own settings.
